correctness.rationale: The degree-one/degree-three threshold reduction is exact for all positive rho. A source set in the middle phase is contagious precisely when at least one rim core is initially seeded and each cyclic gap between seeded cores has no more than one completely unseeded core-leaf pair; two such pairs block infection permanently, whereas zero or one allows inward propagation. In the high phase every pair must be initially seeded at least once, and leaf-only pairs must be independent, which is also sufficient. These iff criteria yield the complete generating polynomials; maximum independent sets and standard cycle counting give all minimizers. The standalone original-graph checker exhaustively simulates all seed subsets on n=3..9 for each phase, independently enumerates polynomials, and passes, but is not used as an infinite proof. Small boundary n=3 and phase boundaries rho=1/3,2/3 are included.

value.rationale: The degree-proportional threshold process is natural on a unicyclic family with mixed degrees. The result determines every contagious source-set coefficient for all sizes and three sharp phases, and all optimizing configurations. Its middle-phase gap obstruction and high-phase independent-set correspondence explain the exact parity-sensitive 2/3n and Fibonacci/Lucas-type counts, giving structural information and reproducible closed-form enumerators rather than a routine substitution into a known bound. There is no claim of a general theorem for arbitrary graphs.
